newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major says could agree tiny EU voting changes.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major says could agree tiny EU voting changes.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major said on Tuesday there may be small areas in which Britain would agree to an extension of qualified majority voting (QMV) in European Union (EU) decision-making if it would lead to concessions.
"One can never be absolutely certain what comes up in tiny areas," Major told a news conference when asked whether he was ruling out any extention of QMV at the June EU summit.
"I don't know if there's some tiny area where there is a good negotiating point to be gained and something conceded to us. So I don't 100 percent rule it out on the tiny area.
"In the big areas I do. There's no question of us ceding further significant movement away from Westminster on qualified majority voting," Major added.

Major, under pressure from within his own party over Europe, has made Labour leader Tony Blair's inexperience of government a key element of his campaign for the May 1 election, saying he would betray Britain's interests at the Amsterdam sumnmit.
But Labour remains stubbornly ahead in the polls -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7768
